subject: MAP + procurement sequencing: BioMedCorp pilot timeline & DPA path
messages:
From: Ellie Marsh <emarsh@biomedcorp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@biomedcorp.com>, procurement@biomedcorp.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + timeline constraints for pilot / MAP request

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the routing options. We want to formalize a short mutual action plan so our procurement and legal teams can see the steps, milestones, and required artifacts. Key constraints from our side:
- We need a signed DPA before we can spin up any production-like evaluation environments (legal requirement).
- Procurement needs an order form and pricing commitment by June 11 to meet our quarter close.
- We plan a 4-week functional evaluation starting as soon as the DPA is signed.

Attached is our RFP excerpt showing deadlines (Biomed_RFP_v2.pdf). Can you share a simple MAP with owners, dates, and acceptance criteria? Also please let us know if Redwood can provide a checklist of the SOC2 / security artifacts so our InfoSec can pre-clear.

Thanks — cc'ing Jared from procurement.

Best,
Ellie Marsh
Head of Digital Products
BioMedCorp

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@biomedcorp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + timeline constraints for pilot / MAP request

Ellie — thanks for the clear constraints and for sharing the RFP snippet. We've sketched a concise MAP and sequencing for the MSA/DPA/order form so your procurement and legal teams can see the path to getting the evaluation live. High-level summary below; attached is an editable MAP (MAP-draft.xlsx).

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- DPA: Redwood provides our standard DPA + SOC2 evidence link — target signature by 2026-06-07. Owner: Redwood Legal (Karthik).
- Order Form (pricing & billing): Redwood to propose order form (trial SKU) and renewals clause — target sign by 2026-06-11. Owner: Mateo (sales) + procurement.
- Environment Provisioning: Once DPA signed, staging cluster deployed (hosted), credentials + test prompts provided — target provisioning by 2026-06-09. Owner: Marissa (CS).
- Eval Window: 4-week functional test starting 2026-06-10 (contingent on provisioning). Acceptance criteria: latency SLOs (<200ms p95 on 8k tokens), embedding quality benchmarks (sample set), and pass/fail checks in our eval harness. Owner: BioMedCorp + Redwood CS.
- Go/No-go: joint review call and a short acceptance checklist at end of eval (2026-07-08).

Notes / Open items:
- If legal needs redlines, please send them early so we can triage. Karthik can do a targeted review and propose acceptable concessions.
- If procurement cannot hit 6/11 for the order form, we can stage an interim pilot agreement but need to coordinate billing.

I've added links to the HubSpot deal HS-98723 and a DocuSign envelope placeholder in the MAP workbook. I'll loop Karthik for the DPA sequence and Marissa for onboarding details.

Attachments: MAP-draft.xlsx (owners, dates, acceptance criteria + DocuSign placeholders)

Next steps:
- Karthik: can you confirm DPA turnaround and whether we can accept redlines limited to data residency and deletion language?
- Ellie/Jared: confirm procurement priority and whether the 6/11 order form deadline is firm.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP + procurement sequencing: BioMedCorp pilot timeline & DPA path

Ellie — quick note from CS on environment and acceptance tests.

We recommend the following concrete acceptance checks so the evaluation is unambiguous:
- Traffic profile: run three 30-minute sessions that mirror your production prompt mix (we'll help synthesize request patterns).
- Latency: p95 <200ms for <2k token requests; p95 <350ms for 8k token tails (measured by Redwood trace).
- KV/Session behavior: confirm KV cache reuse across repeated chat sessions (we'll provide a test harness).
- Quality: run 50 labeled prompts (shared doc) and measure pass rate >= 80% against your rubric.

We can provision a hosted staging cluster (shared training data stays with you) once the DPA is signed. SOC2 docs: we have an artifacts page and an evidentiary zip we can drop into a secure Drive link. I'll include the SOC2 artifacts link in the MAP workbook and flag any configuration steps for data residency (region: us-west-2).

I'm available for an onboarding call 6/8 or 6/9 to set up the harness.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP + procurement sequencing: BioMedCorp pilot timeline & DPA path

Thanks — that format helps. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:
1) Legal will want to review and likely redline the DPA on data deletion timeframes and subprocessors. Are you able to accept a 30-day deletion requirement for ephemeral tenant logs and provide a subprocessor list?
2) Procurement is asking whether the order form can include a 30-day pilot SKU with an option to convert to a committed monthly package (no automatic renewal).
3) We will try to meet the 6/11 commercial sign date but need to confirm internally — if we miss it we need to push the pilot start two weeks.

Attached is a short procurement schedule we use (Procurement_Schedule_BioMed.pdf). I'm looping Jared to confirm the 6/11 gating.

Ellie

Ellie / Jared — thanks for the clear asks. Quick sequencing guidance from Redwood Legal to keep your procurement timeline intact:

1) DPA first (recommended): we can provide our standard DPA and SOC2 evidence today. Please share redlines within 48 hours if possible. We generally accept targeted changes on data deletion and subprocessors; a 30-day deletion request is more aggressive than our typical 60-day standard, but we can escalate for an exception if the deletion scope is narrowly defined (ephemeral logs only).

2) Order Form next: to meet 6/11 we suggest signing the DPA and a placeholder order form (pilot SKU, 30-day term) concurrently. The order form can include a simple option to convert to a committed monthly package with a signed amendment later. This avoids blocking provisioning.

3) MSA: MSA can be executed either before or after the pilot start depending on your procurement constraints. If MSA gating is strict, we can run on a pilot addendum that references standard MSA terms and auto-supersedes when full MSA is executed.

Proposed dates (if procurement is flexible):
- 2026-06-05: DPA sent to BioMed legal (DocuSign envelope created).
- 2026-06-07: DPA signed (target).
- 2026-06-09: provision staging cluster (after DPA).
- 2026-06-11: order form signed (pilot SKU).
- 2026-06-10 to 2026-07-08: 4-week evaluation window.

If you want to expedite, I can set up a 1-hour legal sync tomorrow to triage the DPA redlines live. Laura will help coordinate the calendar — Laura, can you propose 10:00 or 15:00 PT slots tomorrow?
